decisions.decision: Which rulings does this plan inherit from plans 1 to 4?
decisions.ruling: Keep the astro/ namespace and the processor name astro/client-side-ts. Credit the MIT code in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md plus a one-line source header in each ported file, test files included. Put the code in src/plugins/astro/, in strict TypeScript. Dependencies follow the user's criterion: a direct dependency is not a concern; port what brings peer ranges or conflicting transitive trees. Deprecated rules are not ported. Each edit unit runs mise x -- mise run code:format --fix before it returns. Each test file connects RuleTester to vitest itself and imports from src/. A ported upstream test case that fails only because ESLint 10's RuleTester or the vitest wiring is stricter than upstream's setup — not because the rule behaves differently — may have its test setup changed (for example, remove a duplicate case, or add a property that ESLint 10 requires). Never change the expected messages, message ids, locations, output or suggestions. List each change as DECIDED; the review unit checks them. A case whose expected result differs stops the run with a QUESTION.
decisions.rejected: A new namespace; a separate package

decisions.decision: Which astro rules do we port?
decisions.ruling: 18 native rules of eslint-plugin-astro 3.2.1: all except the deprecated no-omitted-end-tags and valid-compile. The 36 jsx-a11y/* wrappers are not ported: they need eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y, a third-party plugin that this package never installed. The 9 rules that the preset enables are among the 18.

decisions.decision: Which packages are kept and which are ported?
decisions.ruling: Port eslint-plugin-astro (peers eslint >=10, typescript-eslint, @typescript-eslint/parser, eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y). Keep astro-eslint-parser 3.2.0 (native compiler; no peers). Add as direct, exact-pinned, bundled dependencies, at the versions installed today: postcss, postcss-selector-parser, synckit, @jridgewell/sourcemap-codec, @typescript-eslint/types (pinned with the other @typescript-eslint packages), @eslint-community/eslint-utils and espree (ESLint itself depends on these two). None has a peer that holds a core package back. @typescript-eslint/parser stays as it is; plan 6 decides it.
decisions.rejected: Port the parser or the small packages

decisions.decision: Do we fix the client-script TypeScript bug in this plan?
decisions.ruling: Yes (the user's ruling of 2026-11-22). Today a consumer repo gets 'Parsing error: Unexpected token as' on TypeScript in the client <script> of an .astro file; the frontmatter parses. The cause (rulings review, 2026-11-22): upstream's configs/has-typescript-eslint-parser.ts picks the processor by whether @typescript-eslint/parser resolves from process.cwd(); a consumer repo does not install it (this package bundles it), so upstream falls back to the processor astro/astro, whose script blocks espree parses. Inside this repo the parser resolves, so the bug does not show there. The fix: the preset sets processor astro/client-side-ts explicitly (D7), and the ported utils/resolve-parser loads @typescript-eslint/parser and espree from this package (the bundle), never from the consumer's cwd. U4 proves it with tests/unit/plugins/astro/client-script.test.ts, which runs from a temp directory outside the repo (realpathSync of a temp dir, as the golden lint test does), and with a TypeScript client script added to tests/fixtures/astro/valid.astro; smoke.mjs lints the fixtures from an install outside the repo.

decisions.decision: Where does the rule configuration live, and how is parity proved?
decisions.ruling: In the astro preset. The plugin index (U4) exports meta, rules (merged from rules/group-a.ts and group-b.ts), processors { "client-side-ts": <processor>, astro: <processor>, ".astro": <processor> } as upstream exports them, and environments; no configs. The preset reproduces flat/recommended without the jsx-a11y and prettier entries: the parser astro-eslint-parser with parserOptions { parser: @typescript-eslint/parser, extraFileExtensions [".astro"], sourceType module }, the globals (node and astro), the processor astro/client-side-ts set explicitly, the 9 astro/ rules, and no-unreachable off; the virtual-file configs are the two presets of D12 a. After U4, lint/problems.json and lint/fixes.json may change only for tests/fixtures/astro/ files and only by the effect of the D6 fix; config/file.astro.json may change only by what D6 needs; the new snapshot config/file.astro__1.ts.json is expected. U4 adds file.astro/1.ts to the PATHS of tests/golden/config.test.ts. Any other golden change stops the run with a QUESTION.
decisions.rejected: configs in the plugin; accept any golden change

decisions.ruling: One review unit after U4, because the change ships runnable code. Execution mode teams, because wave 2 has two edit units; if a team cannot start, the run uses solo.

MINOR: the D6 fix changes behavior (TypeScript rules now check .astro client scripts), and the deprecated rules and the jsx-a11y wrappers are removed; a scan of ~/Projects on 2026-11-22 found no consumer config that names them.

decisions.decision: Round 1 rulings review: preprocessors, style-lang cases, type shims, --version, versions, the golden path, the client-typescript test
decisions.ruling: (a) utils/resolve-parser loads @typescript-eslint/parser and espree from this package (D6); the transforms keep loading sass, less, stylus and postcss-load-config from the consumer cwd (requireUserLocal), because they are the consumer own style toolchain and are not bundled. (b) The 5 upstream no-unused-css-selector cases invalid/style-lang01..05 need those preprocessors and a postcss config; U3 does not port them and lists each as DECIDED, and U1 does not copy their fixture files. (c) U1 writes src/plugins/astro/shims.d.ts with local declare module entries for less, sass, stylus, postcss-load-config and source-map-js (the types the transforms use); no package is added. (d) U4 narrows the /^@typescript-eslint\// pattern of src/cli/commands/version.ts so that @typescript-eslint/types is not listed and @typescript-eslint/parser still is. (e) U4 pins each new dependency at the version that pnpm-lock.yaml resolves today (for example postcss 8.5.33, postcss-selector-parser 7.2.1, @typescript-eslint/types 8.73.0), read from the lock file, not from a stale node_modules. (f) The golden PATHS entry is the fixed path file.astro/1.ts. (g) The ported client-typescript integration test imports @typescript-eslint/parser directly in place of upstream has-typescript-eslint-parser.ts.
decisions.rejected: Resolve parsers from the consumer cwd; add the preprocessors as devDependencies; add @types packages; list @typescript-eslint/types in --version; pin the stale node_modules versions

decisions.decision: Round 2 rulings review: the virtual-file configs, their registration, the integration test config, the reproduction build
decisions.ruling: (a) The virtual-file configs are required: ESLint skips a processor code block that no files pattern matches. U4 writes src/config/presets/astro-client.ts with two presets, name astro-client-js (files ["**/*.astro/*.js"]) and name astro-client-ts (files ["**/*.astro/*.ts"]), each with the languageOptions of upstream astro/base/javascript and astro/base/typescript at v3.2.1 (the browser globals; for TS, our bundled @typescript-eslint/parser and the parserOptions upstream sets), without prettier/prettier. (b) U4 registers both in composeBaseConfig() (src/config/index.ts) right after the astro preset, and adds them to tests/unit/presets.test.ts; consumers can target them in overrides by these names; U6 adds them to the preset lists of CLAUDE.md and readme.md. (c) Where an upstream integration test uses configs.base, the ported test uses the same shape built from our plugin: the astro preset entry with rules {}, plus the two client presets; upstream expected messages then stay valid. Where it uses configs.recommended, use the astro preset entry as it is plus the two client presets. (d) U4 reproduces the bug with the worktree own build (pnpm run build) before step 2, run from a temp directory outside the repo; the temp directory is not a repo path and needs no owns entry.
decisions.rejected: Optional virtual-file configs; an array preset; createConfig() in the integration tests; a separate checkout of main

decisions.decision: Round 3 rulings review: style-lang06, the parser-resolution details, rules on the client presets, the U4 order, the 95octane ignore
decisions.ruling: (a) All six preprocessor cases, no-unused-css-selector invalid/style-lang01 to style-lang06, are skipped with their fixture files (D11 b covers 06 too). (b) In utils/resolve-parser: @typescript-eslint/parser and espree come from this package (D6); the @babel/eslint-parser fallback stays consumer-local through requireUserLocal; the _ESLINT_PLUGIN_ASTRO_MODULES test hook is dropped; getInstalledParserId stays, reading the bundled parsers; the Module._cache lookup of ESLint own espree in espree.ts is replaced by a direct import of the bundled espree. (c) astro-client-js and astro-client-ts carry rules {}, so tests/unit/presets.test.ts holds. (d) U4 follows this order: 1 build and reproduce; 2 plugin index; 3 the astro preset, astro-client.ts, the registration and presets.test.ts; 4 the dependency change; 5 version.ts; 6 the integration tests; 7 the regression test; 8 valid.astro; 9 the golden PATHS. (e) The ignore of **/*.astro in 95octane is out of scope: it is another repo, and the release is a separate hand step; it is a Parked follow-up.
decisions.rejected: Port style-lang06; keep the test hook; a test exception for presets without rules; an after-landing edit of another repo

decisions.decision: How are eslint-disable comments for unknown rules and strict-TypeScript errors in ported code handled?
decisions.ruling: (a) A ported file may drop an eslint-disable or eslint-enable comment that names a rule this repo does not define, or rewrite it to the rule of this repo that it means; ESLint 10 reports an unknown rule in such a comment as an error, so code:lint would fail. (b) Where the repo's strict TypeScript (noUncheckedIndexedAccess, verbatimModuleSyntax, .js import extensions) rejects ported code, a unit fixes it only with changes that have no runtime effect: non-null assertions, casts, type annotations, import type, and .js or /index.js on relative imports. No runtime guard is added. List each kind of change as DECIDED. (Ruled for all B08 plans on 2026-11-22, from the rulings review of plan 6.)
decisions.rejected: Define the unknown rules; add runtime guards
